answer: A national pension fund signs a challenge binding one contribution record to an agent's key. Each fund holds one record per citizen, checked against its registry every epoch, and a second key claiming the same record is rejected. Forging 1,000 identities means buying 1,000 real contribution histories at about $200 each in back-payments and fees, roughly $200,000, plus a paper trail no attacker can fabricate. The spiral of fake accounts collapses when the delta between claimed and real contributors is audited, and a gale of cheap sybils cannot survive a check rooted in decades of payroll data.
